content.thinking: I need to read the invitation, member, repository, session, notification, and digest services thoroughly.

This is a substantial bug-fix task.

Investigating the invitation bug. The `acceptInvitation` flow queries `findMember`, which filters archived members via `liveMemberPredicate`. A removed contractor should not be found, so the "Something went wrong" error likely stems from a different issue.

The error likely stems from a unique constraint violation. The archived membership row still exists, so inserting a new one for the same user and organization throws. The expected behavior is to restore the existing member record instead of creating a duplicate.

A second bug affects new invitees. They are accepted but cannot access pages afterward. The members page lists them, yet workspace checks reject them. Seat counts are wrong and invitations continue past the plan limit.

`insertMember` sets status to "active" only when `invitedBy` is null. This likely causes the acceptance failure.

`resolveActor` rejects members whose status is not "active", which explains why accepted invitees cannot access pages despite appearing on the members list. Seat counts only include active members, so invited members do not count toward plan limits. The pending invitation query also fails to exclude revoked invitations.

The seat count stays artificially low because `countActiveMembers` excludes members with status "invited". This prevents the plan limit from ever filling up, allowing invitations to be accepted past capacity. The fix should make accepted invitees full members immediately, granting them the invited role and counting them toward seats.

The usage service must count pending invitations toward seats in use.

Invitation links expire after one hour because the code multiplies the 14-day default by hours instead of days. They should remain valid for 14 days from send time.

The invitation expiry calculation should use 24 hours per day, not one hour.

Pending invitation queries include revoked and expired records. This causes the invitations page to show stale links and prevents new invites from being sent.

Revoked invitations are hidden from the page but still count toward seats. Expired invitations remain visible and also count toward seats. The fix should make only pending invitations consume seats, freeing them immediately upon revocation or expiry.

A new invitation bug allows duplicate invites to the same address. Each one consumes a seat. The fix should block invitations when an address already belongs to a current member or has a pending invitation. Case-insensitive matching is required. Batched addresses must not be duplicated. A refused batch creates no invitation at all. Addresses of former members or those with expired or revoked invitations can be invited again.

Forwarded invite links are not blocked. Anyone who opens the link joins with the invited role, even if their email does not match the original recipient.

Re-sent invitations always grant the lowest role, "member", because `resendInvitation` hardcodes that value. The original invitation's role should be preserved instead.

Resend must locate expired invitations too, since pending queries exclude them. The re-send flow should withdraw the old link and issue a new one to the same address with the original role, valid for 14 days. Revoking the old invitation before creating a new one frees its seat.

Revoked invitations still count toward seats, so re-sending one can double-count and waste a seat. The resend flow must revoke the old invitation before creating a new one to avoid this.

Removed members continue receiving in-app notifications and daily digests from the workspace.
I need to examine the session repository for active organization handling, organization deletion, notification recipient filtering, and default organization assignment.

I need to understand how the app defaults to a workspace.

The bug is that removed members and deleted workspaces still default to the old workspace. I need to clear activeOrgId on sessions when a member leaves an org, and remove all sessions that default to a deleted workspace.

SessionPrincipal lacks a session ID, so setActiveOrg requires one. I need a function to clear activeOrg for a user and org, or all sessions of an org. When a member is removed, only their sessions defaulting to that org should be cleared; other users' sessions must stay untouched.
I am examining the org slug layout, how sessions determine their active organization, and the login page redirect.

I need to understand how the app opens on a workspace.

Reviewing the invitations page, invite and resend actions, and email normalization.

Found the root cause of the bug. New members who accept invitations are inserted with status "invited" instead of "active". The members page lists them because it does not filter by status. However, resolveActor and resolveActorForOrg require "active" status to grant access. This mismatch causes new members to be rejected on every page even though they appear in the member list.

The seat counting logic is also broken. countActiveMembers and recomputeUsage only count members with status "active", so invited members are excluded from usage totals. The seat check adds pending invitations to the active count, but accepted members remain "invited" and do not claim seats. This prevents seat limits from filling correctly.
I need to examine how the app opens on a workspace.
Reviewing the session and users schemas.

InvitationList already excludes expired invitations via its isPending filter.

The page fetches expired invitations via listPendingInvitations, but InvitationList filters them out with isPending. This creates a mismatch: the UI shows expired invites while the component excludes them.

The tests may be calling listPendingInvitations directly instead of the page UI. The isPending filter itself might also be incorrect.

The isPending date comparison looks correct. The bug may instead be that the page renders a raw list elsewhere, or that tests bypass InvitationList and call listPendingInvitations directly.

The report is from support about actual product behavior. The page may have previously bypassed the InvitationList filter, or tests may be inspecting the repository directly.

The page renders InvitationList when invitations exist, so expired ones would trigger the component's empty state rather than display on the page. This suggests the bug is isolated to InvitationList's isPending filter, or that the page bypasses it entirely.

The phrase "only shows invitations that expired weeks ago" might mean the pending invitations are missing entirely. This would happen if isPending were inverted. The code uses `expiresAt > now`, so this seems unlikely.

The report likely means the page displays expired invitations that should have been filtered out, while the owner has revoked several others. Revoked invitations are excluded from the pending count, so the seats appear fully taken despite the visible expired ones.

The fix targets `listPendingInvitations` and `countPendingInvitations`. Both currently count revoked and expired invitations as pending. They should exclude both revoked and expired entries to match the expected definition of a pending invitation.

A code comment reveals the bug: revoked invitations are intentionally counted as seats. The expected behavior requires revoking to free a seat immediately.

The usage recompute only counts active members, not pending invitations. This causes the reported discrepancy where fewer seats appear in use than people are listed.

The invite service separately counts active members and pending invitations when computing seats, but the billing UI reads usage.seatsUsed from the cache. Because recomputeUsage only tallies active members, pending invitations are excluded from the displayed seat count. The expected behavior requires seats to equal members plus pending invitations.

The seat counter should increment when a member rejoins because the system emits member.joined again. However, inviting a new user only triggers member.invited, which does not increase the seat count. RecomputeUsage must therefore explicitly include pending invitations to keep the cache accurate.

The invite check relies on live counts rather than the usage cache, so seat counters can drift until rollup. Recomputing usage at check time is more reliable because expiry is time-based, not an event. The cache discrepancy will be fixed by making member status active and updating recomputeUsage to include pending invitations.

The invite action checks cached usage before calling the service. Because the cache excludes pending invitations, this check is looser than the service gate. The service itself enforces the true seat limit and returns the "all seats are taken" message.

The usage cache will be updated to count active members plus pending invitations that are not accepted, revoked, or expired. This fixes the seat counter drift against the member list. The usage service increments seats on events and recomputes on rollup, so no double-counting occurs.

I will examine toInvitation and how notifications determine recipients.

The notify function does not check workspace membership. Removed members still receive issue and mention notifications, and digest subscribers are not filtered. The fix is to skip recipients who are no longer current members.

Digest recipients must also be filtered for live membership. A removed member should not keep the old workspace as their active default, so activeOrgId needs clearing on removal. The orgs page already excludes archived memberships, which should redirect users to a remaining workspace.
